title: DMG MORI NLX 2500 - CNC Machining Our FIRST PART, 3.0" dia 6Al-4V Titanium, Vlog #15

controller_features: Context-sensitive controls (auto mode shows program controls, jog mode shows rapid access)
Modal soft-key interface (relevant buttons shown per operation mode)
machine.notes: First part ever made on this machine by Tyson. DMG MORI service tech praised the work. Live tooling spindle goes to 10,000 RPM with good horsepower. Machine described as 'so dialed' that tool marks are nearly invisible.

material.name: Ti-6Al-4V
material.notes: 3.0 inch diameter, 8 inches long Ti-6Al-4V bar stock. This is the most common aerospace titanium alloy, classified as ISO Group S (heat-resistant superalloys).

software.notes: CAM system not explicitly named in transcript. Programming done by Tyson. Part is a complete single-operation (done-in-one) setup combining turning and live tooling milling.

operations.operation_name: OD rough turning with DNMG insert

tool.notes: DNMG 55-degree diamond insert. Diamond shape allows undercuts and access to tight geometry. Can rough out most of the OD profile in a single tool.

cutting_parameters.notes: 70 thou (0.070 in) depth of cut at 200-250 SFM for OD roughing Ti-6Al-4V. These are moderate-aggressive parameters for titanium turning.

operations.strategy: Rough as much OD as possible with DNMG insert, utilizing the diamond shape to reach undercuts. Then step down for deeper features.
operations.notes: Main OD roughing tool. 70 thou DOC at 200-250 SFM is a solid, production-proven parameter set for Ti-6Al-4V roughing on a rigid machine like the NLX-2500.

operations.operation_name: OD grooving with 0.125 inch wide insert

tool.notes: 0.125 inch (1/8 inch) wide grooving insert in a cartridge-style holder. Same holder body used for face grooving by swapping cartridge.

operations.strategy: Groove multiple features including OD grooves. Insert also used to rough out areas the DNMG cannot reach. Finishes the middle groove and surrounding features.
operations.notes: Grooving holder uses interchangeable cartridges - same holder body, different blades/inserts for different groove widths and orientations.

tool.notes: Full radius insert for profiling the center section of the part.

cutting_parameters.notes: 79 thou depth of cut mentioned for this tool. Used for the center profile section.

operations.strategy: Machines the entire center section of the part profile.
operations.notes: Full radius profiling tool handles the complex center geometry that other tools cannot efficiently reach.

tool.notes: Dedicated finish tool separate from roughing insert.

operations.strategy: Finishes as much of the OD as possible - comes across the top, then steps down to finish the back end of the part.
operations.notes: Achieved 25.1 microinch Ra surface finish on titanium, as-machined with no polishing or deburring. This is an excellent finish for Ti-6Al-4V turning.

tool.notes: Same grooving holder body from operation 2, but with a different cartridge installed for face grooving orientation.

operations.strategy: Finishes the inside features and face grooves. Roughs and finishes everything on the inside that it can reach.
operations.notes: Interchangeable cartridge system saves turret stations - one holder body, multiple insert cartridges for different operations.

operations.operation_name: Upside-down boring bar for ID features

tool.notes: Boring bar mounted upside-down with a slight angle. Inverted orientation allows it to function as a grooving tool for internal features.

operations.strategy: Finishes roughing the remaining internal features, then finish passes to blend with previous operations.
operations.notes: Upside-down boring bar mounting is a clever technique to reach features that a conventional boring bar orientation cannot access. The angled orientation enables it to groove internally.

operations.operation_name: Live tooling milling with 4-flute end mill

tool.notes: 4-flute end mill for roughing milled features. Used in live tooling spindle.

operations.strategy: Mills flats/pads across the face and stepped features on the sides using C-axis positioning.
operations.notes: Live tooling spindle runs at up to 10,000 RPM. This is where the turning center transitions to milling mode for features that require it.

tool.notes: Ball end mill for finishing contoured surfaces created by milling operations.

operations.strategy: Final surface finish pass on milled features.
operations.notes: Ball mill provides smooth surface finish on contoured milled features.

od_roughing_titanium.calculated_rpm_note: RPM = (SFM x 12) / (pi x 3.0). At 200 SFM: 255 RPM, at 250 SFM: 318 RPM. As diameter reduces, RPM increases to maintain constant SFM.
od_roughing_titanium.assessment: 200-250 SFM with 0.070 DOC is a solid production parameter set for Ti-6Al-4V roughing on a rigid turning center. This aligns well with industry recommendations of 150-300 SFM for carbide inserts on titanium depending on grade and coating.

profiling_titanium.assessment: 79 thou DOC for profiling is slightly deeper than the roughing DOC, suggesting this tool handles a specific geometry where deeper engagement is needed.

surface_finish.post_processing: none (no polishing, deburring, or secondary finishing)
surface_finish.assessment: 25.1 microinch Ra on Ti-6Al-4V as-machined is excellent. Typical specification for aerospace titanium finish turning is 32-63 microinch Ra. Achieving 25 microinch without secondary finishing demonstrates both machine rigidity and well-chosen finish parameters.
surface_finish.notes: Measured by scribing a profilometer across the surface. Presenters were impressed with the result.

workholding.description: Single setup (done-in-one) operation — all turning, grooving, boring, and milling completed in one chucking
workholding.notes: 3-inch diameter, 8-inch long titanium bar held in chuck. All operations (OD turning, grooving, profiling, ID boring, live tooling milling) completed in a single setup. This eliminates re-chucking error and is ideal for tight-tolerance aerospace parts.

advantages: Quick change — pop out, pop back in, no need to re-touch off
Ball lock provides rigid, repeatable connection
Crash protection — adapter breaks before turret damage
Just offset after insert change, no full tool touch-off needed
tooling_system.notes: KM50 holders praised for quick-change capability. When changing inserts, you just pop the tool out, swap the insert, pop it back in and offset — no need to completely re-touch the tool. This saves significant setup time in production.

process_strategy.description: Complete part machined in single setup combining 6 turning/grooving/boring operations followed by 2 milling operations using live tooling. Sequence: OD rough -> groove -> profile -> OD finish -> face groove -> ID boring bar -> end mill -> ball mill.
process_strategy.rationale: Single-setup strategy eliminates re-chucking error on aerospace titanium part. Turning operations handle all rotational features first, then live tooling handles milled features (flats, pads, contours). Interchangeable cartridge grooving system maximizes turret station usage.
key_techniques: DNMG diamond insert for maximum OD roughing coverage including undercuts
Interchangeable grooving cartridges to save turret stations
Upside-down boring bar for internal grooving access
Full radius insert for complex center profile
Live tooling with 10K RPM spindle for milling operations
Done-in-one eliminates setup error on 8-inch long part

tribal_tips.tip: For Ti-6Al-4V OD roughing on DMG MORI NLX-2500, use 200-250 SFM with 0.070 inch DOC using a DNMG (55-degree diamond) insert — production-proven parameters for titanium turning
A DNMG 55-degree diamond insert can reach undercuts and tight geometry on OD turning — use it as the primary roughing tool to remove maximum material before switching to specialty tools
25.1 microinch Ra surface finish is achievable on Ti-6Al-4V as-machined (no polishing) on a well-dialed DMG MORI NLX-2500 — far exceeding typical 32-63 microinch aerospace specs
Use interchangeable cartridge grooving holders to save turret stations — same holder body with different cartridges for OD grooving and face grooving operations
Mount a boring bar upside-down with a slight angle to use it as an internal grooving tool — allows access to features that a conventional boring bar orientation cannot reach
KM50 quick-change tooling on DMG MORI NLX-2500: when changing inserts, just pop the tool out, swap the insert, pop back in and offset — no full re-touch-off needed
For 8-inch long Ti-6Al-4V parts, a done-in-one strategy (all turning + live tooling milling in single setup) eliminates re-chucking error critical for aerospace tolerances
The DMG MORI NLX-2500 live tooling spindle runs at 10,000 RPM with good horsepower — sufficient for milling titanium with end mills and ball mills directly on the turning center

When first setting up a new CNC lathe, start with a moderately complex part that exercises all capabilities (turning, grooving, boring, milling) — builds operator confidence across all machine modes before tackling harder projects

DMG MORI MAPPS IV controller uses context-sensitive soft keys — in auto mode it shows program controls, in jog mode it shows rapid access controls. This reduces button clutter and speeds up operation.
Use a 4-flute end mill for roughing milled features on titanium in live tooling, followed by a ball end mill for finish contouring — same strategy as dedicated milling centers

When accidents happen on a lathe (e.g., accidentally spinning the turret and clearing something), KM50 ball lock interface provides crash protection — the adapter breaks away before the turret is damaged
